- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.3) over recent days, model tends to underreact — adjust forecast upward by 1–2% of recent mean or 0.5–1.0 price point.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.1) and price is falling, model often overcorrects downward — avoid sharp drops; add 0.5–1.0 price point upward bias.
- Model frequently underestimates price spikes in the 3rd–5th day of a new trend — add 0.5–1.5 price point buffer to early forecast peaks.
- Model overestimates mean reversion in 30-day horizon — reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5 price point if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.
- If sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.2–0.4) and price is trending, model often lags — shift forecast 1–2 days ahead with slight upward bias.
- When sentiment is high and price is near 30-day high, model tends to overpredict — cap forecast at 1.5–2.0 price point below recent peak.
- Model underestimates price in 30-day horizon when sentiment is low and price is near 30-day low — add 0.5–1.0 price point upward bias.
- If sentiment is high and price is falling, model often misreads sentiment — add 0.5–1.0 price point upward bias to counteract pessimism.
